name: Little Scribble Workers
description: Five small labours in the margin. Delicate pencil figures build a page as you scroll, and undo their work when you return.

options.label: The little crew · three character studies

assets.credit: Original articulated figure studies and architectural linework

compatibility: Modern desktop Safari, Chromium and Firefox with SVG, ResizeObserver and native scrolling. No GPU, CDN, font or runtime dependency.
Touch uses normal vertical scrolling. Actors are inert, pointer-transparent overlays inside reserved illustration areas. All text and controls use HTML.
Reduced motion starts paused. The timeline, activity selector and finished-page control remain available. Autoplay requires a deliberate click.
Offscreen and hidden previews stop autoplay. Disposal removes all listeners, observers, animation frames, actors and target styles.
notes: Each job is a pure function of progress. The tool, articulated pose and page output use the same state, with no accumulated physics or random frame flicker.

Five completed hammer strokes drive nails and extend a divider. The ladder alternates planted limbs. A ratcheted pulley lifts an actual HTML picture. The pencil traces its actual path. Three carried beams build a frame.
Characters have angular faces, broken garment contours, cuffs, shoes and seeded crosshatching. Jacket, long-coat and apron studies retain the same contact geometry.
The scrollable notebook is a demonstration webpage with five sections. Scrolling is native, with no wheel or touch cancellation. Scrubbing, presets and reverse movement evaluate the same tracks.
reuse: Open example.html from the source ZIP through a local HTTP server; no installation or build is required.
Use createMarginWorker with an attachment element, activity, output target, trigger, position, scale and optional sequence range.
Supply normalized progress yourself, or let the adapter observe a normal document or container scroll trigger. See embed-demo.html for a native document example.
model.js is DOM-free; drawing.js owns the contours; worker.js owns attachment and output; index.js is only the notebook demonstration. README.md documents integration and lifecycle.
